newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM IN NEW BIG RACE CLIFF-HANGER.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM IN NEW BIG RACE CLIFF-HANGER.

text.p: Bosra Sham faces a re-run of her tense 1,000 Guineas countdown this weekend as it emerged the high-class filly has bruised her foot again.
But trainer Henry Cecil remains hopeful that she will make the line-up for Saturday's Newmarket Champion Stakes -- one of the last group one tests of the year in Europe.
Cecil said: "She has got a bruise and there is a pressure point, but she is as sound as a bell.
"We have had to make a gap to take the pressure off the bruise. It's a situation we could do without but I am very hopeful she will be okay.
"I never like these sorts of things happening but she is terribly well in every way and we have to hope."

Despite a similar injury scare in May, Bosra Sham eventually made the 1,000 Guineas line-up and won the race in fine style. But the effort took its toll and she was off the track until the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes last month when she was a creditable second to the 2,000 Guineas winner Mark of Esteem.
Halling, the hot favourite, has won 12 of his last 14 races and is the only horse ever to win the York Juddmonte International and Sandown's Eclipse Stakes twice.
Ridden by Frankie Dettori for the Godolphin operation of Sheikh Mohammed, Halling will be a tough nut to crack.

Timarida, who captured the Irish Champion Stakes for the Aga Khan, has won 10 races in five different countries, but she suffered an infection earlier in the week and might not be at her absolute peak.
Best of the outsiders may be Glory of Dancer, a good fourth in the Epsom Derby, and ridden by Olivier Peslier who partnered Helissio to an outstanding victory in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.
Latest betting: Evens Halling, 7-4 Bosra Sham, 5-1 Timarida, 10-1 Even Top, 12-1 First Island, 25-1 Glory of Dancer, 33-1 Tamayaz, 40-1 Wall Street.
